answer: Attention-Challenge Gating works by requiring each identity to answer a fresh task drawn from a juniper-tagged queue and hold a session open for a randomized delay before its next action counts. A single missed challenge resets the identity's crystal counter to zero, so the enforcement rule ties every transaction to sustained, verified presence rather than a one-time credential. Because each fake identity must burn real wall-clock attention on its own separate challenge stream, an attacker's cost scales linearly with the number of identities held above the ridge needed for useful throughput.
